titulo: The last day — check out, leave the bag, and say the thing that makes you welcome back
subtitulo: Checkout is administrative. The goodbye is not, and it is the sentence people actually remember
cena: The room is empty, the flight is at nine tonight, and the person at the desk has been the same face all week.
frasePiso: Settle the bill, park the bag, and then say one true sentence to the person who helped you all week.

steps.pt: The last morning has two halves. The paperwork, which is quick, and the goodbye, which is the part you will remember.

steps.promptPt: Open the checkout in one sentence. Speak now.
steps.pt: Good morning, I'd like to check out.

steps.es: Certo. Ha preso qualcosa dal frigobar?
steps.pt: Of course. Did you take anything from the minibar?
steps.tts: Certo. Ha preso qualcosa dal frigobar?
steps.acao: Answer honestly, then ask for the itemised bill anyway.

steps.pt: Answer that one honestly and read the bill anyway — the tourist tax lands here, and it was never in what you prepaid.

steps.promptPt: Ask to see the itemised bill before paying. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I see the itemised bill?

steps.encaixe: lasciare la valigia fino alle sei
steps.promptPt: You have a whole day and a suitcase. Ask, with the time. Speak now.
steps.es: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei?
steps.pinyin: POS-so la-SHA-re la va-LEE-ja FEE-no AL-le say
steps.pt: Can I leave the suitcase until six?
steps.tts: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei?

steps.es: Certo, gliela mettiamo nel deposito. Nessun problema.
steps.pt: Of course, we'll put it in the store room. No problem.
steps.tts: Certo, gliela mettiamo nel deposito. Nessun problema.

steps.promptPt: Check whether the left luggage costs anything, using the frame from B11. Speak now.
steps.pt: How much does the left luggage cost?
Now the part that is not administration. Say something specific — specific is what separates thanks from a formula.

steps.promptPt: Tell them you were very comfortable here. Speak now.
steps.es: Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto.
steps.pinyin: see-A-mo STA-tee be-NEES-see-mo, GRA-tsee-eh dee TOOT-to
steps.pt: We were very comfortable, thank you for everything.
steps.tts: Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto.

steps.promptPt: Name the thing that actually helped: their advice about the restaurant. Speak now.
steps.es: Il ristorante che ci ha consigliato era ottimo.
steps.pinyin: eel ris-to-RAN-te keh chee a kon-see-LYA-to EH-ra OT-tee-mo
steps.pt: The restaurant you recommended was excellent.
steps.tts: Il ristorante che ci ha consigliato era ottimo.

steps.es: Che piacere sentirlo. Torni a trovarci!
steps.pt: How nice to hear. Come back and see us!
steps.tts: Che piacere sentirlo. Torni a trovarci!

steps.promptPt: Answer that properly — say you'll be back. Speak now.
steps.pt: We'll definitely be back. Until next time!

steps.promptPt: Ask them to get you a taxi to the airport, using the frame from B14. Speak now.
steps.es: Mi chiama un taxi per l'aeroporto?
steps.pinyin: mee kee-A-ma oon TAK-see per la-e-ro-POR-to
steps.pt: Could you call me a taxi to the airport?
steps.tts: Mi chiama un taxi per l'aeroporto?

steps.es: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei? Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto. Alla prossima!
steps.pinyin: POS-so la-SHA-re la va-LEE-ja FEE-no AL-le say. see-A-mo STA-tee be-NEES-see-mo GRA-tsee-eh dee TOOT-to. AL-la PROS-see-ma
steps.pt: Shadow the last morning: the bag, the thanks, the goodbye.
steps.tts: Posso lasciare la valigia fino alle sei? Siamo stati benissimo, grazie di tutto. Alla prossima!

steps.pt: B18 done, and ME VIRO with it. You can arrive, eat, buy, sleep, get help, and leave in a way people remember.

secoes.corpo: Grazie di tutto is fine. Naming the actual thing — the restaurant, the room they moved you to, the umbrella they lent you — is what turns a transaction into a relationship you could pick up next year.
Hotels routinely hold luggage after checkout, usually free for guests, and stations and city-centre services do it for a fee. Asking for it turns a dead last day into a real one.

The tourist tax, the minibar and any extras land on the final invoice rather than the prepaid booking. Asking for the itemised version is not distrust — it is the only moment when a question still has an easy answer.

secoes.titulo: The journey ends in a goodbye
secoes.corpo: This module opened with a greeting you gave before you needed anything. It closes with one you give when you no longer need anything. That symmetry is the whole point: the language was never only for extracting things.

permissao: You are allowed to say something warm on the way out, in imperfect Italian, to someone you will probably never see again. That is not sentimentality — it is the last and easiest use of everything you learned, and it costs one sentence.
espelho: Anyone who has left a hotel with a nod and thought afterwards that they should have said something to the person who fixed their week knows this small regret. It is not a language problem; the sentence is just easier to skip than to say.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You thank the front-desk person warmly and they say torni a trovarci — come back and see us.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: A polite formula, like have a nice day, that does not need a real answer.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: It is a formula, but one that expects the return shot. Leaving it unanswered lands as a conversation dropped rather than closed, in a culture where the closing exchange carries real weight.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer it: torneremo di sicuro, or simply alla prossima. Two words finish the exchange properly.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You leave having had a small conversation instead of having received a pleasantry, which is also how you get remembered if you do come back.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when you genuinely will not return and saying so would be a lie you have to maintain — grazie di tutto on its own is a complete and honest close.
